messages:
Terry L: Customer hit onboarding friction — copied README curl and got 401 "insufficient_scope".
Evie N: Which sample? quickstart or sample-app?
Terry L: Quickstart. They copied: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","input":"hello"}'
```
Marcus F: Likely two issues: scoped API keys now require inference.write for POST and sample-app env var is sometimes REDWOOD_KEY in code. Docs drift.
Terry L: Quick wins: add a one-line note above curl about required scope and fix env var name in the sample app. Also link to SDK retry guidance for token rotation.
Evie N: I'll open a tiny PR that: (1) inserts comment `# make sure key has inference.write scope`, (2) replaces REDWOOD_KEY -> REDWOOD_API_KEY in sample app, (3) adds a one-line changelog entry at top.
Docs Bot: docs-ci: running spellcheck + linkcheck for PR #1302.
Marcus F: For parity, add a minimal Python retry snippet under Advanced so Python users have same guidance as Node. Example: 
```python
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from urllib3.util import Retry
retry = Retry(total=4, backoff_factor=0.2, status_forcelist=[429,500,502,503,504])
session.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retry))
# or set SDK client.retry = retry if supported
```
Evie N: Good. I'll ping @Marcus F for snippet review and merge after CI green.
Terry L: Thanks — please keep the changelog line short: "2026-03-08: clarified auth scopes, env var names, and retry guidance." :thumbsup:
